During regional planning sessions, the AOE shared a preliminary methodology for identifying the costs of mental health services and sought feedback from education leaders. Section E: Analysis & Reporting.Data Request: E.1. Report on Act 46 local decision criteria and the State Board’s final plan
E.2. Report on prior analysis regarding what constitutes "geographic isolation"
E.3. Explanation of how AOE identifies economic disadvantage for setting the tax rate
E.4. Explanation of how AOE identifies economic disadvantage for reporting assessment data
E.5. Explanation of how AOE identifies economic disadvantage for allocating federal dollars to public districts
Section E: Analysis & Reporting.Notes:
One thing we would want to make clear to the committee is that federal education funds must always be supplemental, and can only be used to support activities that would not otherwise be provided by the LEA in the absence of these federal funds. The amounts and availability of these grant funds are subject to change based on Congressional actions and cannot be predicted with certainty. Therefore, district configuration decisions should be made without reliance on federal funds.
Public Schools:
•	Title IA allocation: Below is a general overview of the poverty data that is used for Title IA funding and how LEAs then use those funds to support students in their eligible schools. 
o	The Census Bureau uses statistical modeling (review their methodology on the census webpage) to estimate populations at the federal poverty level for each LEA in the state. US Ed uses these Census Bureau poverty estimates to determine eligibility and allocations for the Title I, part A program for each LEA. Currently, all LEAs in Vermont are receiving some Title IA funds. Title I, part A allocations are made up of four individual formula grants. LEAs with larger census poverty rates are eligible for more formula grants. LEAs with larger enrollments receive larger amounts within the formula grants for which they are eligible.
o	Once eligible VT LEAs receive their allocations, they will determine which of their public schools are eligible to be served with Title IA dollars based on the low-income rates of students enrolled in their schools. The determination of which schools are eligible for Title IA services is based on the percentage of their students that are from families at or below 185% of the federal poverty level. This is determined based on data sources such as Medicaid direct certification data, FRL or Household Income forms, etc. LEAs have the authority to distribute their Title IA dollars to all eligible public schools or to concentrate their funds at the schools with the highest poverty rates. 

•	Title IIA & IVA allocations
o	All VT LEAs receive a Title II, part A allocation which is based in 80% on their Census Bureau poverty estimates, and 20% on their enrollment size. 
o	LEAs who received a Title I, part A allocation in the prior year will receive a Title IV, part A allocation in the current year that is proportional to the LEA’s prior year Title IA allocation.

Section E: Analysis & Reporting.Data Request: E.6. Explanation of how AOE identifies economic disadvantage for allocating federal dollars to private schools
Section E: Analysis & Reporting.Notes:
Independent Schools:
LEAs must also serve eligible independent schools with Title funds. The list of eligible approved or recognized non-profit independent schools can be found here.  
•	Title IA equitable services: For Title IA services, LEAs consult with independent school leaders to determine which, if any, of their residents (living in public Title I school attendance areas) are attending an independent school and which of those students are considered low-income. The ESEA permits an LEA to use any or a combination of the following data sources to qualify students attending Independent Schools as low-income: 
	The same measure of poverty used to count public school children (i.e. Household income form)
	Comparable poverty data from a survey
	Comparable poverty data from a different source
	Proportionality
	An equated measure
o	The LEA has the final authority to decide which method(s) it will use.
•	Title IIA and IVA equitable services: 
o	For Titles IIA and IVA, the proportion of the LEA’s allocation that must be reserved for services to independent schools is based on the total enrollment of the independent schools within their geographic boundaries (refer to the list of approved or recognized independent schools).
